Twenty-three comments

This name has already been used as an alt. for the Drunken Sailor but this is the tune that’s in O’Neill’s and recorded by both Joe Burke and Andy McGann as Galway Bay, so I hope it’s ok to use it.

I’ve relied on the McGann recording. If you like his use of double stops you could try |:[B3D3]c [d3F3]f| for the first bar of the A and |d [g2d2] [g2d2]| for the last bar of the B part.

The Democratic

Someone asked in a discussion thread what people played with The Rights of Man. I remember someone playing this with it (not what I use myself - that’s Kemp’s, to be submitted soon).

I’ve known this tune ever so long. But now I discover that it’s from Kerr’s Merry Melodies Vol II. There, it is in G minor, but since I’ve always thought of it (and, as far as I know heard it played this way) in Eminor, that’s what I’ve used here.

The Democratic
Someone asked in a discussion thread what people played with The Rights of Man. I remember someone playing this with it (not what I use myself - that’s Kemp’s, to be submitted soon).
I’ve known this tune ever so long. But now I discover that it’s from Kerr’s Merry Melodies Vol II. There, it is in G minor, but since I’ve always thought of it (and, as far as I know heard it played this way) in Eminor, that’s what I’ve used here.

Paddy Carty Transcription

I have done a transcription of Paddy Carty’s version of this tune this afternoon. It’s a quick job but consists of most of the important elements in his playing. If anybody is interested, feel free to email me and I can send you on a MuseScore file with the score attached. It would be too much hassle for me to write it out in ABC with all of the ornaments and such included.

Galway Bay, X:6

This seems to belong in the Pride of Petravore / Rights of Man / King of the Fairies stable of tunes. Nice to throw in as a contrast to some of the lighter, major scale hornpipes. Or maybe just put all the minor / dorian ones together - fill yer boots!

Taken from ‘A Fine Selection of Over 200 Irish Traditional Tunes for Sessions’, compiled by David Speers with a Forward by Matt Cranitch.

↳ Posted by Eubonian on January 26th, 2019.

Galway Bay, X:7

This is Matt Molloy’s version from his cd “Back to the Island” (https://thesession.org/recordings/6041)

youtube link : https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yQHCDGnXDXI

The A part is a lot like the other settings posted here but the B part has some differences.

Throughout the A part except for the last two measures, Mr. Molloy uses the cross fingering on the c natural, causing it to be a bit to sharp and to have an effect similar to what a c# would achieve.

Galway Bay, X:11

Monster tune in any key but in G Dorian it’s dark.
There’s a lot of ways to play it, so I wrote it out long ways.
( Can start with the B pattern or the G shapes….. )

This is a flute setting. Bars B5 and 6 are hard, but worth it.
Good workout for D# and Bb and Fnatural keys.

I was inspired to learn this setting ( or something like it ) from Rennie Pearson’s flute playing.

↳ Posted by Pat Higgins on May 13th, 2022.

Galway Bay, X:13

Somewhat based on Martin Hayes tutorial in https://youtu.be/wGRWLsbssrI
For flute/whistle players who don’t have a keyed flute or find it too hard to half hole etc, This version can be played on a B flat whistle to get the key which has two flats (B flat and E flat) like in Martin’s video. Hopefully it’s clear. Since I’m flute/whistle player, I’m used to reading of all notation as if it were describing the pitch and fingering of a D flute/whistle. Hard for me to transpose on the fly. So I have written this version just to show the fingering of how I would play it on a D whistle, but if used on a B flat whistle it would sound as the key with the 2 flats.
